intro: Stopword filtering removes a supplied vocabulary from tokenized text. Retaining repetition matters because later frequency-based features still need the number of surviving occurrences.
task: Remove exact stopword tokens while retaining repetition and original order.
requirements: Both inputs are sequences of strings, including optional empty strings. Return tokens not exactly present in stopwords, preserving order and repetitions. Matching is case-sensitive; do not normalize or deduplicate output.
Sequence inputs are Python lists or tuples of at most 1000 items. Text inputs contain valid Unicode scalar characters and at most 10000 characters.
Return the documented Python output types and preserve all caller inputs. Raise ValueError for invalid inputs unless the task explicitly reports a record-level rejection.

hints.title: Handle the boundary
hints.body: Build output by walking tokens so source order and duplicates survive.

explanation: Stopword filtering removes a supplied vocabulary from tokenized text. Retaining repetition matters because later frequency-based features still need the number of surviving occurrences.
The policy is explicit rather than language-dependent. Case folding or punctuation stripping must happen in a separate stage if a pipeline wants those behaviors.
